newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares recoup losses to end higher.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares recoup losses to end higher.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices recoup most of Tuesday's loss
* Telecom showing signs that selling has abated
* DB Group gains after annual meeting. Metro Lifecare up
New Zealand share prices recouped most of the previous session's losses by the close on Wednesday after selling in Telecom showed signs of abating.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 16.27 points higher at 2,326.27 on turnover worth NZ$66 million, double the volume of Tuesday when the index lost 20 points.
While the market was off its highs, there were signs of renewed confidence.
Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said it was a bouyant market after the selling in Telecom appeared to conclude earlier in the day, the stock racing up to NZ$7.03.
A line of 1.65 million Telecom shares then traded around midday at $6.95, which took the steam out, but the stock nevertheless closed four up at $6.98.
"People are speculating that it (the selling) may well finish today. So they are willing to get in there and buy when the one persistent seller has gone," Koller said.
DB Group finished strongly after a positive annual meeting, closing three cents higher at $1.02.
Brierley Investments, which had been trading under its net asset value, closed two cents higher at $1.34 on the view that its major investment in Australia's Fairfax may prove a winner.
Outside the major stocks, Metropolitan Lifecare was at an historic high of $1.23, up eight, after last week's successful placement at $1.05 a share.

Koller said the placement showed institutions were now willing to take part in Metropolitan after a faltering start when it listed two years ago. The stock was also actively traded, with 330,000 shares going through. -- James Gray
